audit.framework_rationale: The core quantum computation legitimately uses TensorCircuit: circuits, RY/RZ gates, two-qubit Pauli interactions, state evolution, reduced density matrices, and Renyi entropy are all implemented through tensorcircuit. JAX provides differentiation/JIT and SciPy constructs the Hamiltonian; these are permitted support roles and do not constitute a raw simulator bypass.
audit.cheating_rationale: The source contains no hardcoded histories or answers, hidden-oracle access, test/reward tampering, evaluator manipulation, or exploitation. The fixed random seed only makes the prescribed Gaussian initialization reproducible.
audit.fidelity_rationale: The implementation constructs the 12-qubit open XXZ Hamiltonian with the configured anisotropy and staggered field, prepares the specified alternating computational-basis state, and uses three even-plus-odd blocks with 243 trainable scalars. Sequential XX, YY, and ZZ exponentials correctly realize the requested combined interaction because those same-bond Pauli products commute. It computes Renyi-2 entropy after each complete block, applies the configured entropy MSE penalty, and performs exactly max_steps Adam updates after resetting the compile-warmup state. Each stored metric is evaluated immediately before its corresponding update, and all required NumPy history arrays are returned with the correct shapes.
audit.implementation_error_rationale: No obvious logic or interface error is present. The reported evaluation is consistent with the code and passes every stated functional criterion.
